define: The point where what you earn covers what you spent, so you are neither losing nor making money.
example: A stall with ₹2,000 of monthly costs keeping ₹7 per cup breaks even at 286 cups.

define: A plan you make in advance for where your money will go, so that spending is a decision and not a surprise.
example: Deciding at the start of the month that ₹600 of your ₹3,000 goes to savings is a budget.

define: Money put into a business so it can operate or grow.
example: Using $50 of savings to buy your first batch of materials is capital.

define: The timing of money actually arriving and leaving, which can differ from what you have earned on paper.
example: A stall can be profitable for the month and still run out of cash on Tuesday if regulars pay on Friday.

define: A UPI message asking you to approve a payment. Approving it and entering your PIN sends your money to whoever asked. Since October 2025 only businesses can send one; requests between two people were switched off.
example: A 'refund' that arrives as a request to approve is money about to leave your account, not enter it.

define: Growth that builds on earlier growth, because returns are added to the amount that keeps earning.
example: Interest earned in year one earns its own interest in year two.

define: What is left from one sale after the cost of making that one unit.
example: Sell for ₹15, costs ₹8 to make, margin is ₹7 per cup.

define: A scam in which callers posing as police or officials keep someone on a video call and demand money to 'settle' an invented case. No real agency arrests or fines anyone over a video call.
example: A caller in uniform who says you must stay on camera and transfer money to a 'safe account' is running this scam.

define: Money kept aside only for things you could not plan for, so one bad week does not become debt.
example: Enough saved to replace a broken phone screen without borrowing.

define: A cost that stays the same no matter how much you sell.
example: Stall rent is the same whether you sell 10 cups or 300.

define: The share of revenue left after the direct cost of what you sold.
example: A ₹7 margin on a ₹15 price is a gross margin of about 47%.

define: The general rise in prices over time, which means the same money buys less.
example: If prices rise 6% a year, ₹100 buys about ₹94 worth of goods next year.

define: The cost of borrowing money, or the payment you receive for lending it.
example: A loan at 12% a year costs ₹12 per ₹100 borrowed, per year.

define: Know Your Customer: the identity check a bank must do before and while it holds your account. It is done through the bank itself, never through a link in a message.
example: A text saying your account will be blocked today unless you update KYC through a link is not from your bank.

define: How quickly something can be turned into cash without losing value.
example: Money in a savings account is liquid; a half-finished product is not.

define: The gap between what something costs you and what you sell it for.
example: Buying at 40 and selling at 100 is a margin of 60.

define: Someone whose bank account is used to move stolen money, often after being offered easy pay to 'rent' the account.
example: Being paid ₹2,000 to receive ₹50,000 and send it onward makes you part of the crime, even if you did not know.

define: Needs are what you must pay for to get through the month; wants are what you choose to.
example: Bus fare to college is a need; a second streaming subscription is a want.

define: One-time password: a short code sent to your phone to confirm that an action is really yours. It works once and then expires.
example: Anyone who asks you to read out an OTP is asking for permission to act as you.

define: The original amount borrowed or invested, before interest.
example: On a ₹1,00,000 loan, the principal is ₹1,00,000.

define: What is left after every cost has been paid.
example: Revenue of ₹10,000 with ₹8,000 of costs is ₹2,000 profit.

define: A square pattern a phone camera can read. In UPI, scanning one fills in who you are about to pay. It is only ever used to pay, never to receive.
example: Scanning a shop's printed code at the counter fills in the shop as the person you are paying.

define: The total money coming in from sales, before any costs are taken out.
example: Selling 400 cups at ₹15 is ₹6,000 of revenue.

define: Selling on credit to people you know, who pay later. Common between small shops and their regulars.
example: A regular who takes chai all week and settles on Saturday is buying on udhaar.

define: Whether one single sale makes or loses money, once you account for its costs.
example: If one cup costs more to make than it sells for, no amount of volume fixes it.

define: Unified Payments Interface: India's system for sending money between bank accounts instantly from a phone.
example: Scanning a shop's QR code and paying from your bank app is a UPI payment.

define: The secret number that approves money leaving your account. It is only ever needed to pay, never to receive.
example: If a screen asks for your PIN so that you can 'get' money, the money is about to leave.

define: A cost that rises as you sell more.
example: Milk and tea leaves cost more when you make more cups.

define: The money a business needs on hand to run day to day.
example: Cash to buy tomorrow's ingredients before today's sales are collected.
